metrics.method: Full history 2026-08-07 to 2026-09-10 (151 messages, ids 1-153 with id 62 missing from the export). 'Questions' counts distinct client asks requiring a reply, not individual messages. 'Unanswered over 24h' counts asks with no substantive answer within a day: the Aug 19 drop, the voice-memo offer, the posting cadence, the invoicing cadence, wire friction, the freeloader screenshots, which IG account the quota feeds, the nude-preview breach, and closure on the Drive fix. max_team_silence_days is the longest run with no ALTR message to the client (2026-08-21 to 2026-08-27); note also a 101-hour near-silence 2026-09-04 to 2026-09-08 containing only two ALTR messages. Promises = explicit ALTR commitments with a verifiable outcome in the chat.

what_client_wanted: Aggressive selling with a girlfriend-experience tone, and her content boundaries respected: 'don't be afraid to be aggressive with selling or pricing, and always be like a gf to them' (2026-08-07) and 'chat team is not allowed to send free full nude previews' (2026-09-04).

A consistent dedicated chatter rotation and an explanation of daily revenue swings: 'let me know about the $800 day and the $300 day' and 'would love to keep a consistent rotation of the same chatters on my profile' (2026-08-28).

A working, non-wire way to pay and a stated invoicing rhythm: 'For invoicing, is it weekly or bi-weekly typically?' (2026-08-17) and 'I need the final invoice and an alternative way to make payments immediately since I cannot wire' (2026-09-08).

Voice contact and a posting cadence agreed with her, not imposed on her: 'Would love to hop on a call with someone just to discuss a few things' and 'would love a couple wall post a day - scheduled out an advance is totally fine - as well as story posts' (2026-08-14).
what_worked: The first two weeks of chatting genuinely delighted her: 'Impressed already with chat omg.. thanks guys. Kill it' (2026-08-07) and 'I am really impressed and thankful for the numbers and efforts in the account. I just want you guys to know that I really appreciate it!' (2026-08-17).

Mica's personalised recovery on 2026-08-31 is the best template on the file: the client refused daily posting at 19:21, Mica reframed at 19:23 with 'that's also why I wanted to have an initial call with you so I could get to know you better, understand your goals and what's realistic for you', relinked Calendly, and the call was booked at 19:29. Twenty days of a self-serve link had converted nothing; one personal message converted in six minutes.

Speed, when anyone chose to apply it: Mayson answered her 2026-09-04 call request in 34 seconds and had a meeting link up within 30 minutes, and the commas.com payment rail took 37 minutes end to end once Derrek approved it. Both prove the earlier delays were oversight, not capacity.

warning_signs_missed: A managed creator changing her OnlyFans password and locking the agency out (2026-09-07) is the highest-value churn signal there is. It was seen by her account manager, asked about once in a group chat, never answered and never escalated to the owner.
Wire friction reported on 2026-08-21 got no reply at all; 19 days later the wire was rejected on the invoice due date and that failure is the first clause of her resignation message.
Every complaint she delivered in a soft register - 'polite side note', 'Not sure why', emoji-padded - was under-triaged. Severity was being read off tone instead of content.
Her first revenue complaint was answered by asking whether she had caused it; 'but okay thanks.' on 2026-08-29 is the moment the relationship visibly cooled and nobody logged it.
The Aug 19 never-sold content drop and the 'I'm back' voice memo she offered on day one were still untouched at 32 days - the onboarding brief was never re-read by anyone.
We issued a 30-reels-a-month quota four days after she told us Instagram was removing everything she posted, and while our own commitments to her were 16 days in arrears.
Two unprompted disclosures of Instagram takedowns (2026-08-28, 2026-08-31) went unowned for 14 days, and the domain we had built to prevent exactly that was never checked.
The owner's goodwill was silently clawed back by billing at the wrong amount (2026-09-01) from a client who then paid it without querying it - a trust failure nobody flagged.

A 4-6x spike in message volume from a previously quiet client (2026-08-28 to 2026-09-04) was read as engagement; its content was 100% open complaints and unanswered questions, and it inverted into silence and then churn within a fortnight.
A client terminating was answered only by billing. No one asked why, offered a call, or escalated to the owner - and she left warm enough that the question would have been answered.
